public_rationale: This is an argument about the sustainability of the AI trade without a defined success condition. Finite financial records cannot establish an infinite requirement. Treating a temporary rally, spending pause or profitable quarter as decisive would impose criteria Zitron did not supply.
limitations: This does not assess whether AI investment is excessive or whether current valuations are sustainable.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: For AI to work out, the equities surge must continue in perpetuity, requiring hyperscaler AI revenues (already small) and capex plus neocloud and lab infrastructure to expand infinitely.

statement.excerpt: For everything to “work out,” the current equities surge will have to continue in perpetuity, which requires both hyperscaler AI revenues — which are already depressingly small — and hyperscaler capex to expand infinitely, along with neoclouds, sovereign clouds and AI labs’ vague infrastructure plans to also expand infinitely.

our_interpretation: The passage asserts that indefinite expansion is necessary for a successful AI investment cycle.

Neither successful investment outcomes nor the duration needed to establish success is defined. Replacing these with a particular stock index, return threshold or observation window would materially rewrite the claim.
The description of revenues as depressingly small supplies no numerical comparison.
criteria.support_condition: No finite observation can establish perpetual expansion or its necessity under the undefined success condition.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A counterexample would require an independently specified meaning of success and evidence that it persists after expansion stops. The passage does not supply that meaning.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: A clarification defining successful outcomes, the relevant companies and a finite period over which expansion must remain necessary.
